$schema: UI copy. Keys are stable identifiers used by scenes; see docs/design/ui.md for canonical menu labels. Placeholders: {name} crew member, {n} number, {item} supply name.

title.name: THE PROXIMA TRAIL
title.tagline: You have died of space dysentery.
title.comingSoon: That part of the Lane opens in a later milestone.
title.hint: Arrows or number keys to choose, Enter to confirm.

travel.auto: Hold Enter or press T to travel until something happens.
travel.autoOn: Traveling... (T or any key to stop)

setup.professionPrompt: Many kinds of people travel the Lane. What will you be?

professions.Corporate Executive: A comfortable salary and no useful skills. Money solves most problems, if you have enough.
professions.Ship Engineer: Modest funds and steady hands. Repairs hold, spare parts last, and the drives rarely quit.
professions.Hydroponics Farmer: Little cash, a green thumb, and rations that go further. Algae likes you.

setup.namePrompt: What are the names of your crew? You are the captain.
setup.nameHint: Type a name, up to 12 letters. Leave blank for the default.
setup.windowPrompt: When do you want to leave Independence Station?
windows: 1 March. Stormy start near Earth, but you beat the flare season.
1 April. Unsettled skies at first. Plenty of margin before the flares.
1 May. Fair skies. Flare season is a coin flip on arrival.
1 June. Fair skies early. You will likely meet the flares at the end.
1 July. Calm start. Flare season will be waiting for you.

advice: Two suits per crew. Space is mostly empty, but the parts that aren't are sharp.
Three drives, four if you like sleeping. One drive is a wish.
Rations: 450 per crew member, if you like eating every day.
Boxes of drone charges are cheap. Five boxes will see you through a scare.
Buy a spare plate, a spare pump, and a spare gyro. Two of each if you can.
Nobody ever came back and said they brought too many rations.
A hull plate is ten credits. A new hull is the rest of your life.
Coolant pumps break on the worst day. The worst day is any day.
A nav gyro keeps you on the Lane. Without one, you are only on a route.
Credits do not eat. Spend them before they spoil, which is never. Spend them anyway.
The Executive can buy it all. The Farmer should buy sense.
The Engineer fixes things. I would still buy spares, if it were me.
I sell what you need. What you want, I sell cheaper at the station farther out.
Skimp on suits and the storms will skimp on you.
mattie.greeting: Welcome to Mattie's Outfitters. I'm Mattie Ostrander. What can I fit you with for the Lane?
mattie.greetingAgain: Back again. Fine. What else do you need before you go?

items.drives: Ion drives are forty credits each. Three or four, and you won't regret it.
items.rations: Rations are thirty cents a day. Buy more than you think, then a little more.
items.suits: EVA suits are ten credits. Two per crew member is the sensible number.
items.charges: Drone charges come in boxes of twenty. A scan uses five. Five boxes is a start.
items.plates: Hull plates are ten credits. I recommend at least one spare.
items.pumps: Coolant pumps are ten credits. If one fails, nothing moves.
items.gyros: Nav gyros are ten credits. A lost ship is a long story.

warnings.noDrives: You will not get far. Buy at least one drive.
warnings.lowRations: That is not a lot of rations. The Lane is long.
warnings.lowSuits: You have fewer suits than crew. I would not leave like that.
warnings.noCredits: You've spent every credit you own. Brave, in a way.

mattie.confirm: That comes to {n} cr. Shall we call it a deal?
mattie.thanks: Pleasure. Mind the hazards, and write if you can.
mattie.cantAfford: You haven't the credits for that. I don't run a charity, though I have been tempted.

clear: You made it across without incident. The ship, for once, is not even dented.
The crossing was clean. You are slightly disappointed to have nothing to report.
Clean crossing. The ship is unharmed, and slightly smug.
You came through without a scratch. The hull is suspicious of its own luck.
scraped: You scraped through, and the ship needs a day to catch its breath.
Close call. The hull sang the whole way through, and you will lose a day.
The hull took a scrape and a half. A day to catch your breath.
You slid through with paint to spare, but the ship wants a rest day.
cargo: The crossing shook loose {n} {item}. They were last seen floating behind you.
You lost {n} {item} in the crossing. The rest of the cargo has opinions.
The crossing shook free {n} {item}. They are somewhere behind you, floating politely.
{n} {item} went out with the tide. Nobody saw them leave.
damage: The crossing damaged your ship. Your {item} is broken.
Something big went by too close. The {item} did not take it well.
The crossing was rough on the ship. Your {item} is broken.
Something struck the hull on the way through. The {item} is the worse for it.
injury: {name} was hurt in the crossing. The suit held, but {name} did not entirely.
{name} took a bad knock coming through. It will take some time to mend.
{name} was hurt in the crossing. A few days of rest should help.
{name} came through with a bad bruise and worse manners.
lost: {name} was lost in the crossing. Nobody saw it happen.
The crossing took {name}. The crew made it through. They are not celebrating.
{name} did not come through the crossing. The crew went quiet for a while.
The crossing took {name}. The ship is lighter, and so is everyone's heart.

arrival.title: New Willamette
arrival.intro: You have reached New Willamette. The sky is the wrong color and the ground is the right kind.

Pathfinder.title: Pathfinder
Pathfinder.line: You crossed the Lane with skill and luck in equal parts. The colony will name a street after you.

Spacer.title: Spacer
Spacer.line: You made it, and you did it competently. The Lane Authority has stamped your papers.

Groundling.title: Groundling
Groundling.line: You made it, which is more than the odds suggested. The colony has a place for you.

reached: You have reached {name}. The ship, remarkably, is still in one piece.
Arrival at {name}. The crew exhales for the first time in days.
{name} ahead, then beside, then behind schedule. You are here.
final: You have arrived at New Willamette. The sky is the wrong color.
New Willamette. You made it, and the paperwork is next.
Landfall at New Willamette. The ground is solid and slightly rude.

death.title: Your journey ends here.
death.allDead: The last of the crew is gone. The Lane keeps going, without you.
death.adrift: Your ship is adrift with no drives. The Lane Authority will log it as a recovery.
death.epitaphPrompt: Write a message for the beacon.
death.beaconSaved: Your message is on the beacon.

guide.title: Learn about the Trail
guide.body: The Lane runs from Independence Station to New Willamette, two thousand megaklicks of buoys, rock, and weather. Pack carefully. Fly sensibly. Keep your suits close.

departure: Captain {name} and crew make ready at Independence Station.
Captain {name} signs the last form and checks the airlock twice.
Captain {name} counts the crew, the crates, and the courage. Close enough.
launch: You cast off from Independence Station. The Lane is two thousand Mk long.
The tether drops and Independence Station shrinks behind you.
Drives lit, hatches sealed. Independence Station recedes.
log.repairStart: You set to work on the {part}.

waypoint.storeLater: The station store opens in a later milestone. Mattie sends her regards.

hazard.title: How will you cross?

desc.thread: Fly it yourself. Fast, free, and exactly as risky as it looks.
desc.shields: Half the risk, and nobody dies. The coolant pump may complain.
desc.tug: Pay a professional to tow you through. Safe, and not cheap.
desc.pilot: A Belter flies your ship for 10 cr, after some days of waiting.

thread: You line up the gap and hold your breath. The ship holds the rest.
You thread the needle. The needle has no comment.
Hands on the stick, eyes on the rocks. Nobody talks.
shields: You raise the shields and lean on the throttle. The pump hums a worried note.
Shields up. You push through like a man shouldering a stuck door.
The shields take the knocks. You take the credit.
tug: The tug takes your line for {n} cr. The captain does not look up from his crossword.
{n} cr and a tow. The tug captain calls it a bargain, from experience.
The tug hooks on for {n} cr and hauls you through, humming.
pilotHire: You pay 10 cr and wait {n} days for a Belter pilot to turn up. Miners keep their own schedule.
A pilot is sent for. Expect {n} days. The Belters call that early.
Ten credits buys a pilot. {n} days buys patience.
pilotArrives: The Belter pilot climbs aboard, nods at your gyro, and takes the stick.
A pilot arrives with a thermos and no questions. She takes the helm.
The Belter docks, sniffs the air, and says 'Move over.'
pilotWait: Waiting for the pilot. {n} days left. The coffee is getting worse.
Still no pilot. {n} days to go. The crew is learning card games.
{n} days left until the pilot. The Belters are never late, only eventual.
pumpStrain: The coolant pump coughs, shudders, and gives up. The shields were a lot to ask.
Under all that strain the coolant pump quits with a small, sad click.
The shields held. The coolant pump did not. It sends its regrets.

blocked.pilotSent: You already sent for a pilot.

route.prompt: Titan Refinery is a fork. Which way past the Kuiper Gate?
route.oortDesc: One more station to shop at. {n} Mk from the Gate to the Heliopause.
route.directDesc: No resupply. {n} Mk from the Gate. The Heliopause is worse this way.

oort: You set course via Oort Beacon. The long way has a shop in it.
Via Oort it is. The buoys are old friends by now.
direct: You set course straight for the Shock. The map calls it ambitious.
Direct. No more stops, no more shops, and no more advice.

route.notYet: You have not reached the fork yet.

station.title: STATION
station.menuHint: Choose what to do at the station.

outfitters.sellHeader: They buy back at these prices:
outfitters.title: OUTFITTERS

talk.empty: The station is quiet. Nobody has anything to say.

rest.prompt: Rest at the station for how many days? (1-9)
rest.bonus: Station beds are better. You recover faster here.

leave.noDrive: You need at least one ion drive to leave.
leave.lastDrive: You need a drive to leave.

bought: Paid {cr} cr for {item}. The keeper counts it twice.
sold: Handed over {item} and took {cr} cr. A poor rate, as promised.
